# phase-032 — Reconcile the stdlib module list in SPEC.md with src/stdlib.rs

## You must change `src/ or docs/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/ or docs/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
src/stdlib.rs:7 declares `pub const MODULES: __FINDING__[__FINDING__str] = __FINDING__["console", "csv", "files", "json", "network", "time"]` and src/analyzer.rs:270 rejects a bare receiver that is neither in scope nor in `stdlib::MODULES` with `Unknown variable`. SPEC.md §Standard Library documents four modules that are not in that list — `text` (SPEC.md:753-760), `math` (762-769), `list` (782-788) and `formats` (797-803) — so `text.uppercase("hi")` fails with `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'text'` and `formats.parse_json("{}")` with `Unknown variable 'formats'`. The functions those sections describe already exist as bare builtins at src/stdlib.rs:22-153 (`uppercase`, `lowercase`, `split`, `join`, `sqrt`, `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `json_parse`, `csv_parse`); they are registered under flat names, not under the module names SPEC.md prints. README.md:120-151 documents only files/time/network/json/csv, which agrees with src/stdlib.rs — so README and SPEC disagree with each other.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Make src/stdlib.rs, SPEC.md and README.md agree on which module names exist, routing the builtins that already exist under the documented names or correcting the documents to the names the code really uses.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-032
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] a test reads SPEC.md and README.md, extracts the module names each documents, and fails when a documented name is absent from MODULES at src/stdlib.rs:7 or present in MODULES but documented nowhere
- [ ] every module name in SPEC.md §12 and README.md §Standard Library is callable, and `rb run` of a file calling each one exits 0
- [ ] where SPEC.md shows a call this parser cannot parse — SPEC.md:785 `list.map([1,2,3], to (x) give back x*2)`, which depends on the function literal of phase-034 — SPEC.md is corrected in this phase and the correction is named in REPORT.md
- [ ] edge tests named edge_* cover: a module function called with no arguments, with too many, and with an argument of the wrong type — each a caught RuntimeError naming the function, never a panic
- [ ] edge tests assert a FAILURE for an unknown module name (`nosuchmodule.read("x")`) — a clean error, not a silent `nothing`
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures and every file in examples/ and modules/ still exits 0 (MathUtils.rb excepted, baselined until phase-024)
